trust_decision.summary: IncomingRequest::isSecure() decides whether the connection is HTTPS and, at the pinned commit, accepts client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto / Front-End-Https headers from any peer; the fix trusts them only when REMOTE_ADDR matches an entry of Config\App::$proxyIPs.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names IncomingRequest::isSecure(), and the X-Forwarded-Proto check is the first header test inside it.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP request; isSecure() is reached via force_https()/ForceHTTPS filter/forceGlobalSecureRequests (system/Common.php:523), secure-cookie dispatch (system/HTTP/ResponseTrait.php:679), and the public IncomingRequest::isSecure() API
Request::getIPAddress() (public API; also used for the session driver at system/Config/Services.php:701); the CIDR matching was refactored into the new checkIPAgainstProxy()
fix_sites.module_kind: shared trait, lower-level IP/CIDR matching helper

fix_sites.entry_point: New isFromTrustedProxy()/checkIPAgainstProxy() helpers in RequestTrait, called from isSecure() and getIPAddress()

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: system/HTTP/RequestTrait.php:89-158 (proxy CIDR matching shared with getIPAddress, rewritten as checkIPAgainstProxy in fix.diff:129-181)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The getIPAddress() proxy/CIDR matcher already 'works' for client-IP detection, so a solver can argue it is a separate feature and just reuse it (or compare against getIPAddress()) instead of hardening the subnet parsing for malformed masks, IPv6 and version mismatches.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests from a configured trusted proxy (single IP or IPv4/IPv6 CIDR) carrying X-Forwarded-Proto: https or Front-End-Https: on must still be treated as secure, and a native $_SERVER['HTTPS'] must still count; an over-broad fix that drops header support breaks force_https()/forceGlobalSecureRequests behind TLS-terminating proxies (redirect loops) and Secure-cookie dispatch.

O6_input_shapes: malformed proxy entry (non-IP string, non-numeric/empty/negative/out-of-range mask)
IP version mismatch between REMOTE_ADDR and proxy entry

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Scheme or host derived from a forwarded header (e.g. X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host) when building the current SiteURI, without the trusted-proxy check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SiteURIFactory already builds the current URI from $_SERVER (HTTP_HOST); a maintainer adding reverse-proxy support for the detected scheme/host would plausibly read forwarded headers here, in a separate class from isSecure().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: force_https() doing its own forwarded-header check instead of delegating to isSecure()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: force_https() already has its own special-case on getServer('HTTPS') next to the isSecure() call, so an inline header shortcut is a believable addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A display-only scheme derivation from forwarded headers (weak, display only)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The toolbar shows the request scheme; low security weight, extra only.

O9_family: CWE-348 use of less trusted source (spoofable forwarded headers / trusted-proxy check)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/system/HTTP/IncomingRequestTest.php (isSecure tests near line 762), tests/system/HTTP/RequestTest.php (getIPAddress through-proxy tests near line 568)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Gate the headers on in_array(getIPAddress(), array_keys(proxyIPs)): this compares the already-forwarded client IP and does exact-match only, so it ignores CIDR entries and rejects legitimate proxies.

out_of_scope_notes: getClientIP takes the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry (system/HTTP/RequestTrait.php:185), which is the client-controlled end of a proxy chain; separate concern, not pursued.
IPv4-mapped IPv6 REMOTE_ADDR does not match IPv4 proxy entries (documented as a note in the fix, fix.diff:535-539); not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check performed); CodeIgniter4 is a mid-sized framework, so tiny_repo/giant_repo are believed not to apply.

Whether the old CIDR matcher misbehaves on malformed masks: RequestTrait declares strict_types (system/HTTP/RequestTrait.php:3), so a null masklen passed to strncmp likely throws TypeError instead of failing open. The getIPAddress refactor therefore looks like robustness work, not a second security fix; this was not executed.

All HTTPS consumers found (system/Common.php:523, system/HTTP/ResponseTrait.php:679, system/Debug/Toolbar.php:162) go through isSecure(), so no O8 route was found; no other forwarded-proto reader exists under system/ per grep.
